metadata.content:
Yes, but deletion needs a governance boundary.
A policy that was ever active has become part of the audit history. Hard-deleting it would destroy evidence explaining why packages were once eligible for policy review. So the safe production rule is:
DRAFT
→ Delete permanently allowed
→ only if never activated
→ only if not referenced by a package

ACTIVE
→ cannot delete
→ revoke first

REVOKED
→ cannot hard-delete
→ retained as governance history

SUPERSEDED
→ cannot hard-delete
→ retained as lineage history
For something like the unused Policy-Doc-Low-Risk@1.0.0 currently sitting as draft, Delete policy is appropriate.
The next narrow milestone should therefore be Governed Draft Policy Deletion, not unrestricted delete.
Add it to the existing policy administration lifecycle:
Create Draft
Activate
Revoke
Supersede
Delete Draft
The delete action should be two-step:
Delete policy
      ↓
This permanently removes Policy-Doc-Low-Risk@1.0.0.
Only unused drafts can be deleted.

Deleting human
[ human:knowledge-governance ]

[ Permanently delete ] [ Cancel ]
The runtime service must reject deletion if:
status != draft
OR
policy has package references
OR
policy has authorization history
OR
policy participates in supersession lineage
And deletion must still return:
packageDecision: null
promotion: null
That gives you cleanup without compromising governance history.
I would implement draft deletion backend → route → Builder client → Delete Policy UI next, then visually validate it against the existing unused draft before moving to supersession.
